dedupe_keys.name: general bikeshare feed specification gbfs and systems catalog

description: The General Bikeshare Feed Specification (GBFS) is the open data standard for shared mobility: a set of JSON files that publish the real-time state of bike share, scooter share, moped and car share systems, such as system information, station locations and status, free-floating vehicle positions, vehicle types, pricing plans, service hours and geofencing zones. It was created in 2014 by Mitch Vars with operators, cities, developers and vendors, is governed by consensus voting and is maintained by MobilityData, with version 3.0 (11 April 2024) the current release and 3.1 release candidates in progress. The repository also keeps systems.csv, a community catalogue of feeds that listed 1,540 systems in 48 countries on 26 September 2026, with auto-discovery URLs and authentication details. Feeds describe single systems at station and vehicle level. The specification and JSON schemas are published on GitHub under CC BY 3.0, free; feeds themselves are published by each operator under its own terms. Caveats: the standard deliberately excludes historical data, so studies must archive feeds themselves, the catalogue is self-declared as incomplete, and some feeds need authentication. GBFS feeds support agent-based and network flow models of micromobility, capacity planning of docking stations and resilience of first and last mile links, and GBFS is the shared mobility counterpart of GTFS, catalogued here.
